title: Use the existing useLocalDayClock seam instead of DateTime.now() in sync_orchestrator_test.dart resume-throttle tests
why: SyncOrchestratorImpl itself reads the clock through the injectable DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() (backed by useLocalDayClock/resetLocalDayClock, built specifically so 'tests can swap it' per date_utils.dart), but these two resume-throttle tests compute their seeded SharedPreferences timestamp from the real system clock instead. The 30s-vs-5min and 10min-vs-5min margins are wide enough that this isn't currently flaky, but it's an unnecessary wall-clock dependency the rest of the suite's own convention exists specifically to avoid, and it silently stops being safe if the throttle window is ever tightened close to a minute.
recommendation: Call useLocalDayClock(fixedClock) in setUp and compute recentMs/oldMs as fixed offsets from the pinned clock, matching the DateTimeFactory convention used elsewhere in the suite.
acceptance_criteria: Resume-throttle tests no longer call DateTime.now()
Tests still pass with useLocalDayClock pinned to an arbitrary fixed instant
